title: Probabilistic computing
summary: Noisy p-bits run a logic gate forwards and backwards, and settle into answers.

ideas.how: tiny switches turn noisy, and p-bits put that noise to work

then: Noise is treated only as a problem to be engineered away.
Probabilistic bits (p-bits) are demonstrated in research labs.
The first thermodynamic and probabilistic chips are taped out and tested.
Projection: probabilistic chips for sampling and optimization, if their gains hold up outside the lab.

challenges.title: Run logic backwards
challenges.task: Clamp the output of a p-bit AND gate and let the inputs find themselves.

ask: How can noise be useful for computing?
What is the difference between a p-bit and a qubit?
